parsed_response.reasoning: Verified mechanism: parseRefreshTokenResponse sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when absent, and when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on it validates against minimumTokenResponseSchema which only requires access_token (plus a number-valued property). The office365 caller does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` and then persists via prisma.credential.update — the spread overwrites the real refresh_token with the literal string. The sync endpoint's response 'should only contain the access token and expiry date' per refreshOAuthTokens' comment, so this path is triggered by design. This destroys the user's refresh token, breaking future re-authorization once sync is disabled. Salesforce happens to preserve the original refresh_token, but office365 and zoom paths are concrete data-loss defects introduced by this diff.

judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites the parsed data's refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token' whenever the response lacks one, and callers persist that data as the stored credential key. The sync response by design contains only access_token and expiry, so with sharing enabled the zoom/salesforce/office365 credential updates write the literal 'refresh_token' over the user's real refresh token, destroying the only material that can re-authorize; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset or the flag reverted, those integrations are permanently broken until each user manually reconnects the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it validates refresh responses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not require `refresh_token`), and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` if missing. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned `tokenResponse.data` is merged into `o365AuthCredentials` via `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`, so the literal string overwrites the real stored `refresh_token` and is then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: o365AuthCredentials } })`. That is data loss and can break future re-auth when sync is disabled. (Note: the diff’s new Salesforce refresh path explicitly preserves the old refresh token, so that part of the finding isn’t fully accurate, but the core defect is clearly present.)
